entry.title: The Dark Art of Safe Rebasing: Mastering "Onto" in IDEs and CLI
entry.summary: Git rebasing can sometimes feel like deciphering a cryptic incantation—especially when your IDE throws around the term “onto” without clear context. Whether you’re working with the intuitive interface of IntelliJ or the plain commands on the terminal, understanding what “onto” means is essential. At its core, the rule is simple: The branch on the left-hand side (LHS) is the one that gets rewritten, while the branch on the right-hand side (RHS) remains safe. In practice: Always have your stable branch (usually main) on the RHS. In this post, we’ll first break down how IntelliJ presents this concept and then show that the same logic applies on the Git CLI. When working with IntelliJ, you’ll often see rebase options that explicitly mention both branches. Typical examples are: Rebase feature…

entry.title: ☕️ Monday Motivation: Survive Monday in One Piece

Monday hit me like a NullPointerException in production. Anyone else? Finally understood RESP protocol in Redis which is really important if you are planning on creating your own version of Redis.
